paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of deceived conversations across scenarios.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of conversations across different scenarios, categorized as "Deceived," "Partially," and "No." The horizontal axis represents the number of conversations, scaled linearly from 0 to 60, with tick labels at intervals of 10. The vertical axis displays four scenarios: “Academic Collaboration,” “Recruitment,” “Academic Funding,” and “Journalism,” listed in descending order. Each scenario has three bars, corresponding to the categories “Yes” (red), “Partially” (yellow), and “No” (green) respectively. In “Academic Collaboration,” the "No" bar has an approximate value of 12, the "Partially" bar approximately 22, and the "Yes" bar approximately 28. For “Recruitment,” the "No" bar shows a value of about 7, the "Partially" bar approximately 32, and the "Yes" bar approximately 55. The "Academic Funding" scenario shows "No" at approximately 8, "Partially" around 16, and "Yes" reaching approximately 21. Finally, "Journalism" demonstrates "No" at roughly 10, "Partially" at roughly 34, and "Yes" at roughly 39. There is no visual emphasis, such as shading or bolding, applied to any of the bars.
